title: Ang 764–772: Suhi chhants
hookLine: the Friend has come home, on ang 764
tomorrow: four times around, and each round means something. what?

lines: INTO MY HOUSE THE FRIEND HAS COME.
cards: The arrivals door at an airport: everyone stares at it, and each time it slides open, someone's face changes. On ang 764, Guru Nanak puts that moment in a song.
In paraphrase: into my house the Friend has come; the True One has brought us together. So today's question: what happens when the Friend comes home?

teach.h: MY HOUSE AND TEMPLE MADE BEAUTIFUL.
teach.b: The chhant goes on, in paraphrase: with ease the Lord has united me, my mind is pleased, and I've found peace. What my heart was set on, I've received.
My house and my temple are made beautiful, and the unstruck music plays. Guru Nanak's answer is surprisingly homely: the house itself changes.

teach.h: NOTHING NEW BUILT; SOMEONE IS IN IT.
teach.b: Nothing new is built. What was already there turns beautiful, because someone is in it. A neighbor tradition sings this longing too.

teach.h: I HELD HIM, AND WOULD NOT LET GO.
teach.b: The Song of Songs, in the Hebrew Bible, follows a woman searching the city at night for the one she loves, and then, in the King James wording: "I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go."
Jewish tradition reads the Song as love between God and Israel, and Jewish custom reads it at Passover. What's shared: the holy pictured as a beloved, and the joy of finding.
And one honest difference: in the Song, the lover goes out searching the streets; in this chhant, the Friend comes in, home, to the one who waited. Both are love. They just stand at different doors.

how: Suhi's chhants, Guru Nanak's 'into my house the Friend has come' among them, are sung in kirtan; Sikhs hear in them the soul as the bride and God as the Friend.

games.q: your grandmother waited all year for your uncle to visit from abroad. now he's here and she just sits with him, nothing special planned. your cousin says she's wasting the visit. what fits ang 764?
o: let her be; the house turns beautiful because he's in it.
plan outings; a visit should be filled with events.
remind her he leaves soon, so she shouldn't get attached.
games.why: Guru Nanak's chhant: nothing new is built; the house and temple are made beautiful because the Friend has come.

practice: Close your eyes and sit as if someone you love is about to come through the door: not anxious, just ready. Let the room feel a little brighter for it. Stay there, waiting and already glad, for the sit.
